title: Which route from one dot to another is the shortest?
description: Two dots, A and B, are marked on a sheet of paper and joined by a zigzag route, a curved route and a straight route. The bends of the first two add extra length, and the straight route is the shortest. Keeko's doubt, that all the routes are equally short, is broken by looking at the bends.
teaching_notes: One idea: the shortest route between two points is the straight one, and it is called a line segment. Watch for students who think that routes joining the same two points must have the same length.

video_script.why: The child sees that among all routes joining two points, the straight one is the shortest, and that this shortest path is the line segment.
video_script.substitution: Draw several routes between the two dots and compare how much each one bends.
video_script.anchor: two points A and B marked on a sheet of paper, joined by several routes
video_script.wrong_answer: all the routes are equally short
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says all the routes are equally short because they join the same two points. The bends of the zigzag and the curve add length, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The straight path is the shortest route

final_answer.value: The straight path from A to B, which is line segment AB
final_answer.spoken: the straight path from eigh to B, which is the line segment eigh B

never_show: the straight path named as the shortest route before the answer beat
maths_rules: Points A and B are joined by three routes: a zigzag, a curve and a straight path.
The zigzag and the curve bend away from the direct way, and each bend adds extra length.
The straight path has no bend, so it is the shortest route from A to B.
The shortest path from A to B, including A and B, is the line segment AB.
Slip: joining the same two points does not make the routes the same length.
video_script.design: One idea: the shortest route between two points is the straight one. The same two dots and the same three routes stay on the board all video. The wrong idea is that all routes are equally short.
